claim: Life Reset: 66 Day Habit (App Store ID 6478942469; subtitle 'Gamified Habit Tracker'; shipped as 'Rise: Life Reset in 66 Days' until mid-2025) by Savvy Tech Limited (bundle build.designand.rise) — 1,232 written reviews, 75 storefronts, 16 April 2024 – 7 September 2026, extracted 2026-09-08, analysed 12 September 2026; a Solo-Leveling-styled 66-day programme app sold behind a hard paywall after a long questionnaire

Method: all 1,232 records read individually in the original language (20+ languages) in date order in 21 chunks; hand-built 111-theme taxonomy in 10 families with explicit boundary rules (B01 price exists vs B02 price disclosed too late; E01 cannot add vs E02 cannot edit; F02 AI criticised vs F03 AI valued; E14 persona misfit vs F09 ideological; C03 refund refused vs I01 support unreachable); classified by working index and resolved deterministically to review_id; 11 integrity assertions (no duplicates, map covers exactly the source set, no unknown IDs, no unassigned, contiguous index, index and ID maps agree); 3,073 assignments, mean 2.49 per review; build refuses to write on any of 22 count-check disagreements; post-write verification of every cited ID; 13-field schema with no missing values; HTML entities (including double-escaped) unescaped for reading only; author never reported; no deduplication (three identical 'Good' reviews from three storefronts, effect < 0.25pp); themes under 10 reviews, all 106 payer reviews, all 40 scam-accusation reviews and all 27 contradictions re-read before publication; causation not established

The written corpus is not the rating corpus and the gap is enormous: 4.7★ from ~12,000 ratings vs 2.77★ written — a ~1.9-star divergence because a quarter of writers never got into the product; 'Do not read 2.77★ as the app's standing. Read it as the standing of the onboarding funnel'; 26.87% (331, mean 1.23★) never used the app — questionnaire, paywall, left; the corpus is young and back-loaded — 73.9% (910) written in 2025, the pre-scale era is 59 reviews

No verifiable price — reviewers quote $1.99/mo to $87, £2–£50, €12–€80, zł45–60, AU$17.98–80, CA$24.99–79.99, ¥3,000–4,500 across 29 months, and the listing's ten price points confirm the range is genuinely wide; payer identification (106, 8.60%) is a floor, not a conversion rate; payers average 1.92★ because satisfied payers rarely mention paying — the payer segment is an inventory of post-purchase failure modes; 28 reviews (2.27%) contain no product content; 27 (2.19%) contradict their own stars (J09), disclosed not re-scored

A well-liked product with a broken front door: among reviewers who got inside, 167 (13.56%, 4.78★) report real behaviour change, 60 (4.87%, 4.55★) praise the level-up mechanic, 38 (3.08%, 4.87★) say the Solo Leveling framing is exactly what they wanted — but 43.67% of the corpus (538, mean 1.49★) attacks how the app is sold and supplies 74.6% of every 1–2★ review: 'The product is not the problem. The funnel is.'

One design decision explains most of the corpus — a 10–20 minute questionnaire in front of a hard paywall: B01 hard paywall, no free use 256 (20.78%, 1.31★), the largest theme of any kind; B02 onboarding completed before price disclosed 156 (12.66%, 1.15★), the lowest mean of any theme above 20; together 48.6% of all 1–2★; consistent across 75 storefronts and 20+ languages and almost always the same sentence — 'I spent 10–20 minutes answering personal questions, signed a pledge, and only then learned it costs money'; 37 (3.00%) add that the ad or listing said 'free', 20 (1.62%) frame it as data collection, 35 (2.84%) name the funnel devices — pledges, 'lock in' repetition, countdown discount — as manipulation
this_app_does: long personal questionnaire + pledge, then hard paywall

claim: The free trial was tested both ways: 90 reviews (7.31%, 1.32★) ask for a trial; none existed for most of the corpus; from 24 January 2026 one appears — 11 reviews (B18) describe being charged immediately on signing up for a stated free trial, and trial-use mentions go from 0.20% to 2.85% — and introducing the trial did not reduce paywall anger, it converted it into billing anger: B01 rose from 17.24% to 34.96% across the boundary and 'advertised as free' from 2.13% to 6.50%; 'A trial that requires a card, auto-charges, and is hard to exit has bought the developer the reputational cost of a trial without the trust benefit'

For people who pay the complaint is rigidity, not price: 80 (6.49%) cannot add their own tasks and 70 (5.68%) cannot edit or remove the generated programme — 9.43% and 15.09% among payers; running is the only cardio (20, plus 10 with injury, disability, asthma or nerve damage — 23 distinct); the wake-up window excludes night-shift workers (31, 23 identifying as shift workers); the weekly ramp reaches 90-minute lifts, 4-mile runs and 2 gallons of water for beginners (20); the day closes at 9pm regardless (10) — these sit at 3–4★, where E01 and E02 peak (17.65% and 14.41% of the 3★ band)

Paying customers report problems at nearly nine times the rate of everyone else and support does not catch them: 97 of 106 payers (91.5%) carry a complaint; reliability in 41.5% of payer reviews vs 13.4% of non-payers; progress reset or lost 14.15% of payers vs 2.92% globally, login failure 11.32% vs 1.30%, overcharged 8.49% vs 0.73%; 21 (1.70%, 1.43★) say support is unreachable — a dead button, a 404, a bouncing address, silence — 10 of them payers; 36 request refunds, 21 refused or ignored, 13 invoke a '66-day money-back guarantee' that several say did not materialise

Reliability is episodic and datable: a launch-crash cluster in October 2024 (D01 37.5% of that window); a 22 May 2025 update that stopped the app opening (D01 + D13 37.8% of the following fortnight, users 20–39 days into a 66-day programme); a mid-June 2025 logout wave (D05 + D04 20.5%, 1.92★); an Aug–Sep 2025 signup-blocked cluster where the name field could not be scrolled past (15); a June 2026 crash-on-task-completion wave (32.1% of that month); crash on launch fell to zero in the most recent era while unspecified bugs rose to 7.9% and a new hero-mode bug theme appeared in 2026

The AI objection is durable and aimed at craft, not function: 53 (4.30%, 1.85★) criticise AI-generated art, copy or book summaries — the only product-criticism theme rising in every era (0% → 4.4% → 4.0% → 5.5%), disproportionately Australian (10.34%) and American (4.66%); reviewers do not object to AI planning (4 praise it) but to paying a premium price for assets they read as uncommissioned — several would recommend the app if the art were commissioned
